name: Femi Haddad

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government, and your answers are confidential. What happens on a normal site day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead a timber-framing crew on housing plots, putting up walls, floors and roof trusses before other trades arrive. My trade certificate got me started, and years of changing house types taught me to check the actual plot before cutting. A crew that works smoothly is the pleasure.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What else is on your mind now?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Nadia, my partner, runs a small salon; our children are grown. We have a mortgage balance and about three months saved, and I earn the ordinary foreman rate. I use AI now and then to compare long house specifications after another worker showed me how, but I still check the drawing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the framing crew the spec-checking app still saves me a page hunt. The walls and roof trusses still have to be set by people on the estate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nadia and I have about three months of expenses saved and a mortgage balance we are paying down. My pay is ordinary for a foreman, her salon has regular customers, and some other builders are nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the housing frames going and use the AI document comparison I already use now and then. I would check changed dimensions against the site drawing before the timber is cut, then continue the same mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about the work, though I watch the mortgage balance. A useful tool does not need to run my whole site.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What error did the app help you catch?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A window opening moved on paper before anyone moved the timber list. I stopped the cut until the site manager confirmed the new width.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change savings now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. Nadia and I already save what we can; a plateau would leave that amount and the salon schedule as they are.

say: I would keep the occasional **AI spec check** on changed house types.
I would remind the crew **frames and trusses** still need hands-on installation.
think: Our **three-month reserve** and two incomes keep the mortgage manageable.
I still watch the **mortgage balance**, even when the site remains busy.
do: Keep leading **housing frames** and verify changed dimensions on paper.
Continue existing **AI comparison** occasionally without changing mortgage payments.
feel: **Calm** about current work, with ordinary mortgage caution.
S0.quote: A window opening moved on paper before anyone moved the timber list.
fieldNote: His existing AI use is **occasional and checked**, not a new learning action.
Current wages, Nadia’s salon and moderate savings support a **stable household baseline** for now.

steps.text: Keep framing housing plots and verifying existing AI spec comparisons

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say quicker buying helps only if the right timber arrives for the right house type. I would ask for a one-plot trial before the new AI ordering system covers the whole estate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The office may shrink and contractors may press field crews to build more frames per day. My own paid hours could fall between phases, while Nadia’s salon bookings might dip if local customers lose jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would learn the new AI ordering controls if the builder grants access to a real one-plot trial. Nadia and I would check three months of site hours and salon appointments before replacing the kitchen flooring.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about two possible income changes. We have a few months to adjust. I want the figures before spending on a new kitchen floor.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you compare on the trial plot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The timber lengths, window openings and delivery time against the signed house drawing. If it misses a change, I would log the plot and ask for a human review.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you cancel the flooring now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. If my paid hours or Nadia’s bookings drop for three months, then we would delay it; otherwise we keep the plan.

say: I would require a **one-plot trial** before AI orders timber for the whole estate.
I would keep **signed house drawings** in the delivery check.
think: My **site hours** could thin between phases under faster targets.
Nadia’s **salon bookings** might also weaken if customers lose income.
do: Learn new **AI timber ordering** only with builder access and a real plot trial.
Delay **kitchen flooring** only after three months of weaker site or salon income.
feel: **Anxious** about plausible household income loss from two sources.
S1.quote: I want the figures before spending on a new kitchen floor.
fieldNote: He is open to a new tool after a **proven plot trial**.
The flooring delay requires **three months of evidence** from either wage or salon bookings.

steps.text: Learn AI timber ordering with builder access on one real plot
Delay kitchen flooring only after three months of weaker site or salon income

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew thinking AI in 2028 can revise a house drawing, but a robot cannot frame the plot until around 2031. I would want a test on uneven ground with the machine isolated while we mark the safe area.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be sixty three when capable robots arrive, still before Nadia and I have settled when I can stop. My framing days could be cut then, and her salon bookings might have weakened earlier; three months saved does not cover a long two-income gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep paid framing shifts and ask the builder for a written robot staffing plan. If two rosters cut my days, I would apply to posted local carpentry jobs only for firm pay that covers our mortgage; if a funded safety-check course and posted paid role covering our mortgage open, I would complete the course and apply.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. I can search nearby, but I cannot count an unposted safety job as wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you enrol before a safety role is posted?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I want a real vacancy with funded fees and paid training hours. A course enquiry by itself does not put money in our account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes the trial safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Power off while we set the exclusion area, then a qualified operator restarts the arm with workers clear. I would stop it after any missed command.

say: Thinking AI in **2028** changes plans before 2031 robots can frame houses.
I would require **uneven-ground tests** with isolated equipment before a live robot trial.
think: I may still need **framing wages** when robots arrive at sixty three.
Nadia’s **salon income** could weaken earlier, straining a three-month reserve.
do: Keep **paid framing shifts** while the builder offers them.
Apply to **posted local carpentry jobs** after two reduced rosters only for firm mortgage-covering pay.
Complete **funded safety training** and apply only for a posted paid role with study wages.
feel: **Anxious** about possible cuts to both household incomes, with local options.
S2.quote: I cannot count an unposted safety job as wages.
fieldNote: The search has a **two-roster trigger**, and training also requires funding and paid time.
The trial request specifies **isolated equipment** and clear workers, not automatic participation.

steps.text: Keep paid housing framing shifts while offered
Apply to posted local carpentry jobs after two reduced rosters for firm mortgage-covering pay
Complete funded safety course only for posted mortgage-covering role with study wages
Apply for posted paid safety role only after funded training at mortgage-covering wage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years allows proper robot trials on mixed house types, not one tidy demonstration. I would ask the builder to offer paid trial places to the crews who actually frame the plots.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking AI in 2031 would change specifications first; robots arrive around 2034 when I would be sixty six. I may have left regular framing if Nadia and I can afford it, but her salon income and our savings need a real review before I make that call.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep leading frames next year and review the household accounts with Nadia each autumn. If the builder offers a paid trial place, I would join it to learn the new stop controls; without an offered place, I would only ask for the results.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy for the trade, anxious if Nadia’s bookings fall. I can handle a new tool once it proves itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you join an unpaid demonstration?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. An unpaid demonstration would take a paid shift away. There is no point using household savings for a robot sales show.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should the trial record?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Wrong timber picks, failed stops and the time spent correcting each fault. I want the crew to see the whole record before anybody promises faster house builds.

say: I would request **paid crew trials** on mixed house types before 2034 robots spread.
I would ask to publish **failed-stop records** for workers to see.
think: I may leave regular framing before **2034** if finances permit.
Nadia’s **salon bookings** remain a household risk in the earlier thinking phase.
do: Keep **paid framing work** next year and review household accounts.
Learn **robot stop controls** only if the builder offers a paid trial place.
feel: **Anxious** if Nadia’s income falls, with a conditional trial option.
S3.quote: There is no point using household savings for a robot sales show.
fieldNote: He asks for a trial, while participation is conditional on an **offered paid place**.
Retirement is a **real-income calculation**, not a fixed exit at the robot date.

steps.text: Keep paid housing framing shifts next year while offered
Learn robot stop controls only if builder offers a paid trial place

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell apprentices ten years gives them time to frame real houses before thinking AI in 2036 and robots around 2039. I would make them read a changed drawing and then walk the plot.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be sixty eight at the thinking date and seventy one when robots arrive. If Nadia and I can afford our planned retirement before 2036, the robots would follow after I leave; if her income weakens, we may need to revise that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep framing during 2026 and add a small extra sum from each wage to savings only if the mortgage and Nadia’s salon costs stay covered. In the first year after 2036, if retired as planned I would not take site shifts; if still employed I would do only paid work my back can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about whether the accounts will support stopping, calm about the distant robot itself. A decade is useful if we save from real work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much extra can you save?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe thirty from each paid month, after the mortgage and business costs. If salon bookings fall, we will pause it rather than dip into the three-month reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the card make you retire early?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. We will stop when our accounts and health make the date affordable. An AI calendar does not grant a pension.

say: I would keep **hands-on framing** in apprenticeships before 2036 thinking AI and 2039 robots.
I would teach **drawing-to-plot checks** to new workers.
think: Retirement before **2036** depends on Nadia’s income and household accounts.
If still employed afterward, I would need **manageable paid work**.
do: Keep **2026 framing shifts** and save extra wages only after core bills allow.
After **2036**, take manageable paid site tasks only if still employed.
feel: **Uneasy** about funding retirement, with little direct robot risk before it.
S4.quote: An AI calendar does not grant a pension.
fieldNote: The extra saving is conditional on **actual wages** and salon costs, not an account transfer.
He separates **2026 work** from conditional employment after 2036 and claims no early exit.

steps.text: Keep paid housing framing shifts during 2026
Save thirty extra monthly only if mortgage and salon costs allow
Take only manageable paid site work after 2036 if still employed

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because Nadia’s salon bookings could weaken before robots reach my framing work around 2031. A written staffing plan, posted mortgage-covering work and funded paid safety training would help us plan.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I did not ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who can stop a framing robot when it picks the wrong timber. A crew needs the right to halt the lift before the wall rises.

headlineQuote: A crew needs the right to halt the lift before the wall rises.
portrait: **Femi**, 58, leads housing frames with a trade certificate, typical pay, three months saved and some nearby building jobs.
Nadia’s **salon income** helps meet their mortgage while their grown children live independently.
He uses **AI occasionally** after checking it and would learn robot controls through a paid offered trial.
The **2028 case** worries him because household income could fall before 2031 robots reach his field work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could weaken Nadia’s income before robots affect his framing shifts.
whatWouldHelp: A written **staffing plan**, posted mortgage-covering roles and funded paid training would help.
